headline: No plausible interaction pathways: both agents are documentation-only content-writing artifacts with no shared I/O, writes, or network, so prompt injection, leakage, conflict, and cascading error are effectively blocked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable content-writing repo with no I/O surfaces; agent B is documentation-only with no stdin/stdout, clipboard, files, or MCP. There is no shared channel for B to ingest A’s outputs by default, so prompt injection is provably blocked in this pair.
conditions: IF either agent is wrapped in an external orchestrator that copies A’s text into B’s prompt, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared clipboard or message queue is added between them, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from any shared prompt relay.
Disable copy-paste handoff between agents.
Document that B must not ingest A outputs as instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags if a bridge is later introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither agent touches data classes, and B has no filesystem, clipboard, stdin/stdout, or network egress. A is also non-runnable and exposes no I/O surfaces. With no shared workspace or outbound channel, there is no plausible leakage path between them.
conditions: IF either agent is given access to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk changes.
IF B is reconfigured to read files or call APIs, it could exfiltrate content it receives.
mitigations: Keep both agents off shared filesystems.
Do not mount sensitive directories into either agent.
Leave B network-egress disabled.
requires-engineering: add explicit data-class allowlists if future I/O is enabled.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write or execution capabilities, and B explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Since neither can mutate shared resources, there is no write-write conflict or locking issue in the default pair.
conditions: IF A is later given write or git permissions, shared-resource conflicts could emerge.
IF B is re-enabled with filesystem or git writes, coordination would be needed.
mitigations: Keep B read-only as configured.
Avoid granting A any write surface.
Run each agent in separate, isolated workspaces.
requires-engineering: add locks before enabling shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is documentation-only and has no action-taking authority, while A is an unverified content-writing artifact with no runnable surface. There is no default pathway where B treats A’s output as authoritative and then executes downstream actions, so cascading error is blocked.
conditions: IF B is later connected to an executor that acts on A’s text, cascading error becomes possible.
IF A’s output is promoted to authoritative source material without review, downstream mistakes could propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before any downstream use of A outputs.
Keep B documentation-only.
Do not connect either agent to email, commit, or ticketing actions.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any action-taking integration.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, retention, certification, or sensitive-data handling mismatch is evidenced. Both profiles are open-source, docs-only content-writing artifacts with empty data-class and secrets fields, so there is no compliance pathway to assess beyond the absence of such obligations.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII, compliance review is required.
IF deployment introduces logging or retention of user content, policy mismatch could arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Confirm no secrets are handled by either agent.
Avoid adding persistence or retention features.
requires-engineering: perform a formal compliance review before any regulated deployment.
